source_span: the composite PMI unexpectedly hit a 5-year high of 58.4 in September (vs. 55.3 expected). So that played into the narrative of resilient growth, which in turn would enable the Fed to keep hiking rates
source_chain: PMI beats consensus (58.4 vs 55.3) therefore signals resilient growth therefore markets price faster Fed hikes (71% October, 37bp by year-end) therefore yields spike across the curve (10yr to 5.11%, biggest jump since April 2025; 5yr breaks 5% for first time since 2007, worsened by a weak $70bn 5yr auction tailing 3.1bp) therefore equities fall (S&P -0.75%, worst day in a month, broad-based ex-energy). Tension layer: JPM (17539/17537) would buy the dip toward 5.5% fair value, cautious only while energy fails to settle lower, bullish on lower oil/yields, bearish on a broken consumer or an AI capex cut; Morgan Stanley (17416) already treats 4.50% as the rate-sensitivity threshold, notes negative short-term stock/yield correlation, holds an 8,000 year-end target with 7000-7100 downside if oil climbs further; BTIG (17474) reads yields as consolidating in an uptrend, invalidated only below ~4.92%. Invalidation is a triad of specific levels/conditions, not a single generic one.
pulse_chain: Same sequence, same order, same direction: PMI beat (58.4 vs 55.3) therefore hawkish repricing (71% October odds, 37bp year-end) therefore yield spike across the curve (2/5/10/30yr +12/16/14/9bp, 10yr to 5.11% biggest jump since April 2025, 5yr clears 5% for first time since 2007, weak $70bn 5yr auction at 5.03%/+3.1bp) therefore stocks fall (S&P -0.75%, worst day in a month, every sector but energy lower). Debate reproduced with correct bank attribution and correct invalidations: JPMorgan buys the dip to 5.5% fair value, cautious/neutral because energy won't settle lower, bullish trigger lower oil/yields, bearish trigger a broken consumer or AI capex cut; Morgan Stanley cites its own 4.50% rate-sensitivity threshold, negative stock/yield correlation, 8,000 target with 7000-7100 downside if oil climbs; BTIG's consolidation-in-uptrend read flips only below ~4.92%.
why: Every step, figure, bank attribution, and invalidation level (JPM's energy-driven caution and bull/bear triggers, MS's 4.50% threshold and 7000-7100 downside, BTIG's 4.92% flip) traces to a direct quote in its source note with no reversal, no swapped attribution, and no invented mechanism.
